text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign minister Tansu Ciller ordered the closure of all casinos in the country because she was angry at allegations her family had connections with gaming institutions.
- The health minister has ordered an investigation into lax practises that allowed people to die unnecessarily in emergency wards.
- Leftist opposition leader says Turkey, faced with a scandal over links between the state, the police and organised crime, is going through the greatest crisis of its 73 years as a republic.
- Islamist prime minister says he will sell off state housing despite a court decision declaring the sale unconstitutional.
- Former interior minister Mehmet Agar, who quit amid a scandal over state-underworld links, is being put under pressure by a series of allegations against him since then.
- Big holding companies are racing to buy up banks.

- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is having his adviser investigated over claims that seven million dollars from a government slush fund intended for Afghanistan's General Rashid Dostum did not reach its destination.
- Iran wants better relations with its neighbour Turkey.
